title: Bridgewater Bank - Data Residency & Compliance Discovery
next_steps: Ethan to send SOC 2 / ISO 27001 package and redwood security whitepaper (link) by 2026-03-06
Schedule technical deep-dive with infra team (SE-led) for week of 2026-03-09
Provision trial account with EU-hosted instance for data residency test by 2026-03-10
Share pilot pricing and Dedicated capacity options (Ethan) by 2026-03-05

Nina Kaur: Prepare sketch of proposed Dedicated topology (VPC peering, KMS) and expected throughput for pilot (due 2026-03-09)

summary: Discovery call to understand Bridgewater Bank's data residency, logging, and compliance requirements for evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments. Key concerns: EU data residency for EU customers, HIPAA applicability for certain product lines, log retention and redaction, KMS/HSM key control, SOC2/ISO documentation, and procurement timeline. Agreed next steps include sending security docs, provisioning EU trial, and scheduling SE-led deep dive.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (latency/cost/isolation)
Logging policy and PII redaction / retention limits
Key management: KMS vs HSM and customer-managed keys
Compliance controls: SOC2, ISO, HIPAA applicability, audit logs and access controls
Procurement and contract timeline for pilot and Dedicated procurement
transcript: Header: 2026-03-04 14:00 ET | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Ethan Brooks (Redwood AE), Nina Kaur (Redwood SE), Mark Davies (CISO, Bridgewater), Laura Chen (Head of IT), Priya Singh (Legal/Compliance), Tom Alvarez (Procurement)
00:00:05 Ethan Brooks: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off at 2pm, hope that time still works for you all

00:00:12 Mark Davies: Yep this works. Thanks Ethan. We just want to, uh, make sure we cover data residency and the compliance bits up front, we have EU customers and some regulated lines so this is high priority

00:00:30 Nina Kaur: Awesome, I'll do the technical framing and then Ethan will cover commercial and next steps. Quick note, transcript may have a bit of noise - apologies for any auto captions mistakes
00:00:45 Laura Chen: No worries. Quick intro from our side — I'm Laura, run infra, we are running core systems in AWS eu-west-1 for EU customers, some US workloads in us-east-1
00:00:58 Priya Singh: Priya here — legal/compliance. We need to validate HIPAA for a couple product lines and overall GDPR data residency plus we require vendor SOC2 and audit logs retention policy
00:01:12 Tom Alvarez: Tom, procurement — timeline is roughly vendor selection by end of March, pilot in April, procurement sign-off in May/June, unless there's blockers

00:01:25 Ethan Brooks: Great, that timeline is helpful. Quick agenda: 1) Understand residency and compliance requirements, 2) talk Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, 3) logging and key management, 4) next steps

00:01:40 Mark Davies: Great. First question: can Redwood guarantee EU data never leaves eu region in Hosted? We had another vendor say 'we route some telemetry to US for analytics' and that's a no for us

00:01:55 Nina Kaur: Short answer: for Hosted API we have region controls — we can pin logically to EU-backed hosting, and for Dedicated/Private you get full isolation. However with Hosted we need to clarify what 'telemetry' is — by default we collect minimal operational metrics but we can offer options to disable certain telemetry or route it to EU-only endpoints
00:02:20 Mark Davies: Okay, can you provide the exact list of telemetry fields? Our legal wants to know if any PII or account identifiers are included in those logs

00:02:31 Ethan Brooks: Yes we'll include a telemetry spec in the packet we send; it's in our SOC2 docs but we'll pull it out separately. We'll also note which fields can be turned off for EU-only configs
00:02:45 Priya Singh: HIPAA — we have a small set of clinical-like data for a pilot product. Can Redwood sign a BAA and support PHI controls?

00:02:58 Nina Kaur: We do support deployments for HIPAA workloads — typically via Dedicated or Private where you have dedicated GPU pools and customer-managed KMS. For Hosted we need to check the policy; historically BAAs are offered on specific hosted plans — I'll confirm
00:03:18 Mark Davies: So Dedicated or Private is the safer path for PHI, right?
00:03:24 Nina Kaur: Correct, Dedicated gives you logical isolation and Dedicated VPC attachments, Private is the full on-prem or VPC-controlled deployment if you need that level of control
00:03:36 Laura Chen: On Dedicated — network architecture question: do you support VPC peering or private link? We can't open public endpoints from prod

00:03:46 Nina Kaur: We support both VPC peering and PrivateLink equivalents depending on cloud provider, and in Private we can do on-prem direct networking. We'll include a sample topology diagram in the follow-up
00:03:58 Tom Alvarez: For procurement we need to know if keys can be customer-managed (KMS/HSM) - our policy requires customer-managed keys for certain datasets

00:04:10 Nina Kaur: Yes, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS; we also support HSM integrations for higher assurance. Hosted: we offer CMEK on select plans but usually with limited support — we'll clarify the exact plans that support CMEK
00:04:28 Mark Davies: Logging retention, we have a regulator requirement that logs be retained 7 years for certain audit trails — can Redwood provide configurable retention and export?

00:04:40 Ethan Brooks: We offer configurable retention windows and can export logs to customer-owned S3/GCS buckets or SIEM via secure transfer. For Hosted we have log retention defaults but can extend for enterprise plans
00:04:55 Priya Singh: Are logs obfuscated or redacted automatically? We need to avoid storing raw PII in logs — can you do on-the-fly redaction or pseudonymization?

00:05:08 Nina Kaur: We have redaction filters you can apply at the ingress point; also you can enable prefix/KV caching which avoids storage of full prompts. For deeper redaction we recommend Dedicated/Private where you control ingestion pipelines
00:05:24 Mark Davies: What about auditability — we need immutable audit logs of who accessed keys and models, and we need to prove no team member has leaked keys

00:05:34 Nina Kaur: We provide audit logging for control plane actions, API usage, and key operations, with RBAC and SSO integration (SAML/SCIM). For Dedicated we can ship these logs into your SIEM and set immutability/retention as you require
00:05:52 Ethan Brooks: +1 on SSO — we integrate with Okta, Azure AD. We also support per-route RBAC if you want to restrict who can call higher-privilege models
00:06:03 Laura Chen: Any certifications? SOC2, ISO? And can we get evidence for our security review?

00:06:11 Ethan Brooks: We are SOC2 Type II and maintain ISO 27001 — we'll attach the attestation and you can do direct security review. We'll include a security pack link in the follow-up (link: https://redwood.example/security/soc2.pdf)
00:06:28 Priya Singh: Great, please include any penetration test reports redacted as needed
00:06:35 Mark Davies: Latency concerns — if we use EU-hosted model variants, what's the expected token latency compared to US? We have SLAs for certain endpoints

00:06:46 Nina Kaur: Latency is primarily network plus model runtime; hosting in eu-west-1 will remove network hop, but some optimized kernels may be region-specific. For Dedicated we can provision capacity in eu to meet latency SLOs. We'll propose expected p99 numbers in the technical follow-up
00:07:05 Mark Davies: We also need model version pinning — we can't have silent upgrades that change behavior mid-flight for regulated use cases
00:07:13 Nina Kaur: You can pin model versions and we support controlled rollouts, canary deployments and automatic fallback to older compatible variants if a rollout has issues
00:07:24 Tom Alvarez: Pricing question quickly — Dedicated vs Hosted cost differences, and if we need EU capacity reserved how does pricing change?

00:07:33 Ethan Brooks: Dedicated is committed capacity and monthly/annual contracts; per-token hosted pricing is lower for on-demand but you lose isolation. EU reserved capacity carries a premium due to region allocation; I'll send sample pricing bands in the follow-up

00:07:50 Laura Chen: One specific: our legal requires that logs sent to Redwood not include full account numbers; we must be able to mask account numbers client-side. Is there guidance on client-side redaction?

00:08:02 Nina Kaur: Yes we provide client-side SDKs and recommend client-side redaction for highest assurance; we can provide sample middleware to strip/mask PANs and sensitive identifiers before sending them to the API
00:08:20 Priya Singh: Regarding GDPR data subject requests, can Redwood delete customer data on request, and is there a data retention delete API?

00:08:31 Ethan Brooks: We support data deletion APIs and retention policies. For Hosted we have a deletion flow; for Dedicated/Private you control data lifecycle entirely. We'll include the deletion SLA in the security pack

00:08:48 Mark Davies: Are there any cases where Hosted would be unacceptable for us? For example, if we need customer-managed KMS and EU-only telemetry, could Hosted suffice or would you recommend Dedicated?

00:09:02 Nina Kaur: Hosted can work for many EU-only needs if the right plan (enterprise hosted with CMEK and telemetry gating) is used, but for PHI/HIPAA and long retention immutable logs, Dedicated or Private is usually recommended
00:09:15 Mark Davies: Understood. Ok, procurement items: Tom, timeline check?
00:09:21 Tom Alvarez: We're aiming to have vendor selected by March 31st. We'll do a security review mid-March once we get the SOC2 and topology. Pilot would be 4-6 weeks
00:09:31 Ethan Brooks: Sounds good. We'll aim to get the docs to you by Friday (2026-03-06) and get an EU trial spun up ASAP
00:09:40 Laura Chen: For the EU trial, we want a sandbox that never exfiltrates logs outside eu-west-1 and pushes logs to our SIEM — is that doable?
00:09:51 Nina Kaur: Yes, we can provision an EU-hosted trial and set logging targets to your SIEM using secure export. We'll coordinate the SIEM ingest details in the SE deep-dive
00:10:05 Priya Singh: Contract terms — our standard addendum requires breach notification within 72 hours and right-to-audit. Are those acceptable?
00:10:14 Ethan Brooks: We can accommodate 72-hour breach notification; right-to-audit is commonly accepted for enterprise deals, we can work with legal to scope it
00:10:25 Mark Davies: One more technical: does Redwood keep request/response payloads for model training or improvements? We cannot allow training on raw customer data without consent

00:10:36 Nina Kaur: By default Hosted may collect anonymized telemetry for product improvements, but we have an opt-out for customer data being used for training. For Dedicated/Private there is no training ingested unless explicitly opted in
00:10:50 Laura Chen: Good. Also we need to know about PIIs in embeddings — if you generate embeddings we need assurance they're not stored in a shared embedding index
00:11:02 Nina Kaur: We isolate embeddings per-customer; for Hosted we can also configure cache policies and TTLs. We'll document the embedding lifecycle
00:11:15 Tom Alvarez: Any references/customers in finance who've done EU-only Dedicated?
00:11:21 Ethan Brooks: Yes, we have several regional banks — we'll include anonymized references and a short case study for an EU Dedicated deployment in the follow-up
00:11:34 Mark Davies: Ok that's helpful. Are there day-to-day ops concerns for our platform team? E.g., upgrades, maintenance windows impacting SLAs?
00:11:44 Nina Kaur: We schedule rolling upgrades with canary windows and we provide maintenance notifications; Dedicated customers can control maintenance windows and we have SLA credits for downtime
00:11:56 Priya Singh: We might request contract language on data residency guarantees, is that something Redwood will include in an MSA?
00:12:05 Ethan Brooks: Yes, for enterprise agreements we can contractually specify region residency and data handling commitments. We'll work with your legal to draft the addendum
00:12:15 Mark Davies: Anything else? I have a list of very specific log fields to check — I'll send that after this call

00:12:22 Ethan Brooks: Perfect. Recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO docs and telemetry spec, propose Dedicated topology and pricing bands, provision EU-hosted trial, and schedule technical deep-dive next week. Action items noted
00:12:36 Tom Alvarez: Thanks all, appreciate the thoroughness
00:12:40 Ethan Brooks: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up by Friday. Bye
00:12:44 Mark Davies: Thanks, bye
00:46:50 [end of recording]
